Build a `ProviderRun`-compatible function (lib/jobs/poll.ts shape) that

when the attempt timeout fires. On error it throws a JobError-shaped object
(the poll loop's `asJobError()` handles it with zero edits).

children.docstring:
── The fal queue run loop (shared by every fal adapter) ─────────────────────
Submit `falInput` to the fal queue, poll until terminal, fetch the result, and
extract the image URL. The SINGLE home for fal's submit→poll→result→extract
flow — every fal adapter (text2img / ref-guided / outpaint) calls this with
its own pre-built provider input. `capability` only flavours error metadata.
Throws a ProviderError on any failure or abort. `message`/`retryable` are left
to makeProviderError's defaults (kind→message map; transient kinds retryable),
which is exactly what every former inline block computed by hand.
Termination (priority order): aborted signal → timeout; MAX_POLLS ceiling →
timeout; COMPLETED → exit; a thrown ApiError from status()/result() → mapped
(fal signals failure by THROWING, never via a "FAILED" status).
children.name: runFalQueue

── Error classification ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

Rate-limit (429) and timeout (408/504) are transient; everything else is
provider_error unless it looks like bad input (422).
Network-level errors with NO HTTP status (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT,
ECONNREFUSED, DNS failure, generic "fetch failed") are transient —
classify as "timeout" (retryable).
children.name: classifyFalError

children.docstring:
Race one provider attempt against a timeout. The timeout is `timeoutMs` — the
smaller of the per-attempt budget (90s) and the job's remaining wall-clock, so
a late attempt can never overrun the 300s job ceiling. A `run()` that runs past
the timeout (e.g. a hung provider) resolves to a `timeout` JobError — TRANSIENT,
so the loop retries it (until the per-attempt cap is exhausted or the JOB cap is
reached). The timer respects fake timers.
ABORT: an `AbortController` is created per attempt. When the timeout fires, the
controller is aborted so the provider (e.g. the fal wrapper) can cancel in-flight
I/O and stop its own internal poll loop immediately instead of running orphaned.
CRITICAL (orphaned-promise / unhandled-rejection): when the timeout wins the
race, `run(job, signal)` stays PENDING. A real provider (Phase-7 fal wrapper) may
REJECT later, after the cut — with no `.catch` that becomes an unhandled rejection
that can crash the worker process. We capture the provider promise and attach a
swallowing `.catch(() => {})` so a late rejection (or resolution) after the
timeout never surfaces.
children.name: runAttempt
